market_pulse.note: Jumped 1,104.02 points (+2.15%) to 52,389.75, recovering ground lost after the midterm elections.
Rose 2.35% to 7,549.94, rebounding from its worst week since April 2025; still about 3.4% below last month's record.
Gained 2.74% to 25,253.14 and moved out of correction territory as chip stocks rebounded.
Fell more than 4% to roughly $87 a barrel as President Trump called renewed strikes on Iran unlikely if talks progress; Brent dropped 5.8% to $92.57.

themes.title: Broad rebound after a rough week
themes.summary: Dip buyers returned after last week's sell-off; all three major U.S. indexes rose 2% or more on the same day for the first time since April.

themes.title: Chip and AI-infrastructure stocks bounce back
themes.summary: AMD surged 13.3% on an analyst upgrade, Micron and Sandisk rose about 6%, and power names such as Constellation Energy (+10.5% on earnings) recovered from last week's data-centre worries tied to the midterm results.

themes.title: Nvidia slides on internal inquiry
themes.summary: Nvidia fell 4.3% after its board opened an inquiry into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a business executive; the company said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

themes.title: Oil drops on Iran diplomacy hopes
themes.summary: Crude fell sharply after Trump signalled restraint on Iran despite fresh shipping attacks; Brent is down from more than $112 at the start of the month.

themes.title: Rate-hike odds stay elevated
themes.summary: CME FedWatch showed futures pricing about an 84% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike in December, while the 10-year Treasury yield edged up to about 4.87%.

sectors.name: Industrials
sectors.note: Led the market, up about 4.6%; Caterpillar rose 7.2% to top the Dow after falling more than 10% last week.

sectors.name: Semiconductors
sectors.note: Rebounded strongly behind AMD, Micron and Broadcom, even as Nvidia fell 4.3%.

sectors.name: Utilities / Power
sectors.note: Constellation Energy jumped 10.5% after beating estimates and raising guidance; NRG Energy and GE Vernova also gained.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: Every sector finished higher, but the group traded against a backdrop of crude falling more than 4%.

watch_list.why: Economists expect a 0.2% monthly rise; the report won't include a year-over-year figure because of last year's government shutdown, and it could shift December rate-hike odds.
The outcome of the review into the CEO matters for the largest AI chipmaker and the broader AI trade.
Oil has swung sharply on diplomacy headlines; any change in the talks or new shipping attacks could move crude quickly.
